steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Strain theory (Merton): society promotes cultural goals (especially material success) but does not provide equal access to legitimate means to achieve them. When people cannot achieve success legitimately, they experience strain. Five adaptations: conformity (accept goals and means), innovation (accept goals, use illegitimate means - e.g. theft), ritualism (abandon goals but follow means - e.g. dead-end job), retreatism (abandon both - e.g. drug addiction), rebellion (replace both with new goals - e.g. revolution).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Labelling theory (Becker): no act is inherently criminal - it becomes criminal only when labelled as such by society. Primary deviance (minor, unlabelled rule-breaking) is normal. When someone is labelled as a criminal, they may accept the label and commit further deviance (secondary deviance), leading to a deviant career and master status (the label becomes their primary identity). Young's study of hippies: police labelling created a deviant subculture.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Subcultural theories: Cohen: status frustration - working-class boys who fail at school form delinquent subcultures that invert school values (they value what the school condemns). Cloward and Ohlin: three subcultural types - criminal (established crime networks), conflict (gang violence for status), retreatist (drug use, both legitimate and illegitimate means failed).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Marxist explanations: crime is a rational response to capitalist exploitation. Working-class crime is caused by poverty and alienation. White-collar crime is caused by capitalist greed. Gordon: capitalism encourages crime at all levels because it promotes self-interest and competition. Chambliss: crime is built into capitalism.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe Merton's strain theory and evaluate how well it explains crime. | Explain how labelling theory accounts for crime and deviance, using Becker's ideas. | Evaluate whether Marxist or Feminist explanations provide a better understanding of crime.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Merton's 5 adaptations: Conformity, Innovation (crime), Ritualism, Retreatism, Rebellion. Strain = goals without means. Labelling: Primary deviance -> LABEL -> Secondary deviance -> Deviant career -> Master status. The LABEL creates the criminal. Marxist: crime is caused by CAPITALISM. Feminist: gender gap is caused by PATRIARCHAL CONTROL of women.
